objective: Test whether a single-network configuration gives fail-closed downbeats as safely as madmom DBN + D3 at materially lower CPU cost.
current_unknown: Whether the two-network D3 candidate can be replaced by a cheaper configuration for mobile.
hypothesis: A single-network configuration meets: silent error rate <= C1 + 0.005, false-alarm rate <= 0.05, cost <= 0.6 x C1.
competing_hypotheses: Beat This! minimal is accurate enough that its own activation contrast suffices (C2).
madmom's own activations suffice without a second network (C3).
Only cross-network disagreement catches silent errors (C1 stays).

stages.output: Configurations, metrics and decision rule pre-registered in commit f3fa43d.
4 configurations x 32 fixtures, per-stage process CPU time at 1 torch thread, 527 s wall.

stages.note: No new mechanism built; the false-alarm traps from GRID-METER-002 (sync_anticip, halftime_switch) are inside the decision set.
Same fixture generator as GRID-METER-002; audio hashes recorded per row for future comparison.

stages.output: No single-network configuration recommended; C1 silent error 0.029 vs C2 0.049, C2 cost 34% of C1 with 0.991 trustworthy coverage.
GRID-METER-003 (real tracks) stays first; GRID-METER-005 cheap second opinion for C2 queued as candidate.

regression_check.detail: Different metric family (silent error / coverage); no direct regression comparison made.

limitations: CPU time on an x86 container core is a proxy; no device, memory or WASM/ONNX measurement.
Small silent-error counts; Wilson intervals of C1 and C2 overlap slightly.

next_recommended_experiment.reason: Real-track error rates may change which configuration matters; still blocked on one human input.

human_interventions: None for this cycle. Device-level cost needs a real phone run.
